authorization_mode.description: Optional. The authorization mode of the Redis cluster. If not provided, auth feature is disabled for the cluster. Default value: "AUTH_MODE_DISABLED" Possible values: ["AUTH_MODE_UNSPECIFIED", "AUTH_MODE_IAM_AUTH", "AUTH_MODE_DISABLED"]
authorization_mode.rationale: Controls whether Redis client access requires authentication. Enforcing IAM authentication supports identity-based access control and prevents unauthenticated client access.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can delete or abandon the cluster. Preventing destructive deletion reduces the risk of accidental loss of service and data.

deletion_protection_enabled.description:
Optional. Indicates if the cluster is deletion protected or not.
If the value if set to true, any delete cluster operation will fail.
Default value is true.
deletion_protection_enabled.rationale: Controls API-level deletion protection for the cluster. Enabling deletion protection reduces the risk of accidental or unauthorised destructive operations.

kms_key.description: The KMS key used to encrypt the at-rest data of the cluster.
kms_key.rationale: Controls whether a customer-managed encryption key is configured for data at rest. Leaving kms_key unset falls back to Google-managed encryption, so policy should require a non-empty CMEK reference with the standard Cloud KMS resource-path structure without pinning any team-specific project, key ring, or key.

labels.description:
Resource labels to represent user provided metadata.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Provides resource metadata for organisation and identification but does not directly configure authentication, encryption, network access, or another security control.

maintenance_version.description:
This field can be used to trigger self service update to indicate the desired maintenance version. The input to this field can be determined by the available_maintenance_versions field.
*Note*: This field can only be specified when updating an existing cluster to a newer version. Downgrades are currently not supported!
maintenance_version.rationale: Selects a maintenance version during an update. Although maintenance releases may contain security fixes, there is no reusable secure value that can be consistently enforced across deployments.

name.description:
Unique name of the resource in this scope including project and location using the form:
projects/{projectId}/locations/{locationId}/clusters/{clusterId}
name.rationale: Identifies the cluster resource but does not directly configure a security control.

node_type.description:
The nodeType for the Redis cluster.
If not provided, REDIS_HIGHMEM_MEDIUM will be used as default Possible values: ["REDIS_SHARED_CORE_NANO", "REDIS_HIGHMEM_MEDIUM", "REDIS_HIGHCPU_MEDIUM", "REDIS_STANDARD_LARGE", "REDIS_HIGHMEM_XLARGE", "REDIS_HIGHMEM_2XLARGE", "REDIS_STANDARD_SMALL"]
node_type.rationale: Controls the compute characteristics and capacity of Redis nodes rather than authentication, encryption, network access, or another direct security control.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the Google Cloud project containing the resource but does not itself configure the cluster's security behaviour.

redis_configs.description:
Configure Redis Cluster behavior using a subset of native Redis configuration parameters.
Please check Memorystore documentation for the list of supported parameters:
https://cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/cluster/supported-instance-configurations
redis_configs.rationale: Provides general Redis behaviour configuration across multiple possible parameters and does not represent a single reusable security control at this argument level.

region.description: The name of the region of the Redis cluster.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

replica_count.description: Optional. The number of replica nodes per shard.
replica_count.rationale: Controls the number of replica nodes and primarily affects availability and capacity rather than a direct security control.

server_ca_mode.description:
The serverCaMode for the TLS enabled Redis cluster.
If not provided, SERVER_CA_MODE_GOOGLE_MANAGED_PER_INSTANCE_CA will be used as default Possible values: ["SERVER_CA_MODE_GOOGLE_MANAGED_PER_INSTANCE_CA", "SERVER_CA_MODE_GOOGLE_MANAGED_SHARED_CA", "SERVER_CA_MODE_CUSTOMER_MANAGED_CAS_CA", "SERVER_CA_MODE_UNSPECIFIED"]
server_ca_mode.rationale: Controls which certificate authority hierarchy issues server certificates for TLS. Requiring SERVER_CA_MODE_CUSTOMER_MANAGED_CAS_CA places certificate issuance under an organisation-controlled CA pool, providing greater control over the trust hierarchy and supporting compliance requirements. The policy constrains only the CA mode and does not pin a team-specific CA pool.

server_ca_pool.rationale: Identifies the team-owned CA pool used when customer-managed CAs are selected. The security decision of whether customer-managed CAs are used is controlled by server_ca_mode, while constraining this reference would require hardcoding project- or team-specific CA pool identities.

shard_count.description: Required. Number of shards for the Redis cluster.
shard_count.rationale: Controls data distribution and cluster capacity rather than authentication, encryption, network access, or another direct security control.

transit_encryption_mode.description:
Optional. The in-transit encryption for the Redis cluster.
If not provided, encryption is disabled for the cluster. Default value: "TRANSIT_ENCRYPTION_MODE_DISABLED" Possible values: ["TRANSIT_ENCRYPTION_MODE_UNSPECIFIED", "TRANSIT_ENCRYPTION_MODE_DISABLED", "TRANSIT_ENCRYPTION_MODE_SERVER_AUTHENTICATION"]
transit_encryption_mode.rationale: Controls encryption of traffic between Redis clients and the cluster. Requiring server-authenticated transit encryption protects data from interception or modification in transit.

automated_backup_config.description: The automated backup config for a instance.

automated_backup_config.retention.description:
How long to keep automated backups before the backups are deleted.
The value should be between 1 day and 365 days. If not specified, the default value is 35 days.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, ending with 's'. Example: "3.5s".
automated_backup_config.retention.rationale: Controls how long automated backups are retained. Retention length is a team data-management and recovery-policy choice rather than a reusable platform security control, unlike deletion-protection settings that directly block destructive operations.

automated_backup_config.fixed_frequency_.description: Trigger automated backups at a fixed frequency.

The start time of every automated backup in UTC.
It must be set to the start of an hour. This field is required.

Hours of a day in 24 hour format. Must be greater than or equal to 0 and typically must be less than or equal to 23.
An API may choose to allow the value "24:00:00" for scenarios like business closing time.
automated_backup_config.fixed_frequency_.rationale: Controls the hour at which automated backups run but does not itself establish a reusable security control.

cross_cluster_replication_config.cluster.description:
The role of the cluster in cross cluster replication. Supported values are:

1. 'CLUSTER_ROLE_UNSPECIFIED': This is an independent cluster that has never participated in cross cluster replication. It allows both reads and writes.

1. 'NONE': This is an independent cluster that previously participated in cross cluster replication(either as a 'PRIMARY' or 'SECONDARY' cluster). It allows both reads and writes.

1. 'PRIMARY': This cluster serves as the replication source for secondary clusters that are replicating from it. Any data written to it is automatically replicated to its secondary clusters. It allows both reads and writes.

1. 'SECONDARY': This cluster replicates data from the primary cluster. It allows only reads. Possible values: ["CLUSTER_ROLE_UNSPECIFIED", "NONE", "PRIMARY", "SECONDARY"]
cross_cluster_replication_config.cluster.rationale: Controls whether a cluster participates in cross-cluster replication as a read/write primary or a read-only secondary. For clusters configured with a primary_cluster source, policy should require cluster_role to be SECONDARY so the replica remains read-only. This enforces a real read/write security boundary rather than merely distinguishing CLUSTER_ROLE_UNSPECIFIED from NONE.

cross_cluster_replication_config.primary.description: Details of the primary cluster that is used as the replication source for this secondary cluster. This is allowed to be set only for clusters whose cluster role is of type 'SECONDARY'.
The full resource path of the primary cluster in the format: projects/{project}/locations/{region}/clusters/{cluster-id}
cross_cluster_replication_config.primary.rationale: Identifies another cluster resource used as the replication source. This is a resource-reference field, and platform policy should secure the referenced cluster itself rather than hardcoding which team-owned cluster this field may name.

cross_cluster_replication_config.seconda.description: List of secondary clusters that are replicating from this primary cluster. This is allowed to be set only for clusters whose cluster role is of type 'PRIMARY'.
The full resource path of the secondary cluster in the format: projects/{project}/locations/{region}/clusters/{cluster-id}
cross_cluster_replication_config.seconda.rationale: Identifies secondary cluster resources that receive replicated data. This is a resource-reference field, so constraining it would require hardcoding team-specific cluster identities rather than enforcing a reusable structural security control.

gcs_source.description: Backups stored in Cloud Storage buckets. The Cloud Storage buckets need to be the same region as the clusters.

gcs_source.uris.description: URIs of the GCS objects to import. Example: gs://bucket1/object1, gs://bucket2/folder2/object2
gcs_source.uris.rationale: Identifies Cloud Storage bucket and object paths used as import sources. These are resource references, and platform policy should secure the referenced storage resources rather than whitelist specific team-owned bucket or object paths.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description:
Optional. Maintenance window that is applied to resources covered by this policy.
Minimum 1. For the current version, the maximum number
of weekly_window is expected to be one.

Required. The day of week that maintenance updates occur.

- DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED: The day of the week is unspecified.
- MONDAY: Monday
- TUESDAY: Tuesday
- WEDNESDAY: Wednesday
- THURSDAY: Thursday
- FRIDAY: Friday
- SATURDAY: Saturday
- SUNDAY: Sunday Possible values: ["DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED", "MONDAY", "TUESDAY", "WEDNESDAY", "THURSDAY", "FRIDAY", "SATURDAY", "SUNDAY"]
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Controls the explicitly selected day for the weekly maintenance window. Because DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED is an accepted sentinel value, policy should forbid that sentinel and require an explicit day to be selected, without mandating a particular day of the week.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description: Required. Start time of the window in UTC time.

Hours of day in 24 hour format. Should be from 0 to 23.
An API may choose to allow the value "24:00:00" for scenarios like business closing time.
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Controls maintenance scheduling only and does not directly affect the cluster's security configuration.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description: Minutes of hour of day. Must be from 0 to 59.
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Controls maintenance scheduling precision only and does not directly affect security.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description: Fractions of seconds in nanoseconds. Must be from 0 to 999,999,999.
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Controls maintenance scheduling precision only and does not directly affect security.

maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.description:
Seconds of minutes of the time. Must normally be from 0 to 59.
An API may allow the value 60 if it allows leap-seconds.
maintenance_policy.weekly_maintenance_wi.rationale: Controls maintenance scheduling precision only and does not directly affect security.

managed_backup_source.description: Backups that generated and managed by memorystore.

managed_backup_source.backup.rationale: Identifies a specific managed backup resource used as a restore source. This is a resource-reference field, so platform policy should secure the referenced backup itself rather than constrain which team-owned backup may be named.

persistence_config.description: Persistence config (RDB, AOF) for the cluster.

persistence_config.mode.description:
Optional. Controls whether Persistence features are enabled. If not provided, the existing value will be used.

- DISABLED: 	Persistence (both backup and restore) is disabled for the cluster.
- RDB: RDB based Persistence is enabled.
- AOF: AOF based Persistence is enabled. Possible values: ["PERSISTENCE_MODE_UNSPECIFIED", "DISABLED", "RDB", "AOF"]
persistence_config.mode.rationale: Controls whether persistent recovery data is maintained for the cluster. Enforcing an approved persistence mode supports recovery following destructive incidents or data loss.

persistence_config.aof_config.description: AOF configuration. This field will be ignored if mode is not AOF.

persistence_config.aof_config.append_fsy.description:
Optional. Available fsync modes.

- NO - Do not explicitly call fsync(). Rely on OS defaults.
- EVERYSEC - Call fsync() once per second in a background thread. A balance between performance and durability.
- ALWAYS - Call fsync() for earch write command. Possible values: ["APPEND_FSYNC_UNSPECIFIED", "NO", "EVERYSEC", "ALWAYS"]
persistence_config.aof_config.append_fsy.rationale: Controls the write durability and performance behaviour of AOF persistence and is not a general authentication, encryption, or access-control setting.

persistence_config.rdb_config.description: RDB configuration. This field will be ignored if mode is not RDB.

persistence_config.rdb_config.rdb_snapsh.description:
Optional. Available snapshot periods for scheduling.

- ONE_HOUR:	Snapshot every 1 hour.
- SIX_HOURS:	Snapshot every 6 hours.
- TWELVE_HOURS:	Snapshot every 12 hours.
- TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS:	Snapshot every 24 hours. Possible values: ["SNAPSHOT_PERIOD_UNSPECIFIED", "ONE_HOUR", "SIX_HOURS", "TWELVE_HOURS", "TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS"]
persistence_config.rdb_config.rdb_snapsh.rationale: Controls RDB snapshot frequency and primarily affects data durability and recovery timing rather than a direct security boundary.

persistence_config.rdb_config.rdb_snapsh.description:
The time that the first snapshot was/will be attempted, and to which
future snapshots will be aligned.
If not provided, the current time will be used.
persistence_config.rdb_config.rdb_snapsh.rationale: Controls when RDB snapshots begin and is an operational scheduling setting rather than a direct security control.

psc_configs.description:
Required. Each PscConfig configures the consumer network where two
network addresses will be designated to the cluster for client access.
Currently, only one PscConfig is supported.

psc_configs.network.description:
Required. The consumer network where the network address of
the discovery endpoint will be reserved, in the form of
projects/{network_project_id_or_number}/global/networks/{network_id}.
psc_configs.network.rationale: Identifies the consumer VPC network that hosts the Private Service Connect endpoint. This is a reference to a team-owned network resource, and constraining which specific network may be named would overreach beyond a reusable platform-level control.

zone_distribution_config.description: Immutable. Zone distribution config for Memorystore Redis cluster.

zone_distribution_config.mode.description:
Immutable. The mode for zone distribution for Memorystore Redis cluster.
If not provided, MULTI_ZONE will be used as default Possible values: ["MULTI_ZONE", "SINGLE_ZONE"]
zone_distribution_config.mode.rationale: Controls whether nodes are distributed across one or multiple zones and primarily affects availability rather than a direct security control.

zone_distribution_config.zone.description: Immutable. The zone for single zone Memorystore Redis cluster.
zone_distribution_config.zone.rationale: Determines the zone used for a single-zone Redis Cluster deployment. As a zone/location field, policy should restrict it to an approved zone whitelist to support organisational data-residency and deployment-location requirements.
